notes.summary: Order and ranking questions give positions in a row or class, or compare people (taller, heavier). Most can be solved with three small formulas and a quick line diagram. SSC asks 0 to 1 question in Tier 1 and Tier 2.

concepts.title: Total from both ends
concepts.body:
If a person is L-th from the left and R-th from the right, the person is counted twice, so:
Total = L + R − 1
Example: Amit is 7th from the top and 26th from the bottom. Total = 7 + 26 − 1 = 32.

And the other way round:
Position from the right = Total − (position from left) + 1
Example: in a row of 40, Ram is 15th from the left. From the right: 40 − 15 + 1 = 26th.

concepts.title: People between two persons
concepts.body:
Both counted from the same end: people between = difference of positions − 1. (5th and 12th from the left: 12 − 5 − 1 = 6.)

Counted from opposite ends (A is L-th from the left, B is R-th from the right, total T):
CasePeople between
L + R < T (no overlap)T − (L + R)
L + R > T (they cross)(L + R) − T − 2
Example (no overlap): 32 students; Priya 18th from the left, Akash 12th from the right. 18 + 12 = 30 < 32, so 32 − 30 = 2 people between.
Example (overlap): row of 20; A 15th from the left, B 12th from the right. 15 + 12 = 27 > 20, so 27 − 20 − 2 = 5.
If unsure, convert both to positions from the left and use difference − 1.

concepts.title: When positions are swapped
concepts.body:
If A and B interchange places, A takes B's old place. So A's new position from the left = B's old position from the left.
Example: Amit is 12th from the left and Sunil 15th from the right. After swapping, Amit is 17th from the left.
  • So Sunil's old place was 17th from the left, and it was also 15th from the right.
  • Total = 17 + 15 − 1 = 31.

concepts.title: Someone exactly in the middle
concepts.body:
If C stands exactly between A and B, the gap from A to C equals the gap from C to B.
Example: Prince is 5th from the right, Amit 15th from the right, and Amit is exactly between Prince and Aditya. Aditya is 6th from the left.
  • Gap from Prince to Amit = 15 − 5 = 10 places, so Aditya is 10 places beyond Amit: 25th from the right.
  • Total = 25 + 6 − 1 = 30.

concepts.title: Comparison ranking
concepts.body:
Write each statement as an inequality with the bigger one on the left, then join them into one chain.
  • "Ramesh is taller than Qadir but shorter than Saurabh" gives S > R > Q.
  • "Tariq is taller than Saurabh" gives T > S.
  • "Prakash is the shortest" puts P at the end.
Chain: T > S > R > Q > P. Tallest: Tariq. Middle: Ramesh.
Watch for "only": "Q is heavier than only T" means Q is second lightest. If some places cannot be fixed, answer only what the chain shows for sure.

concepts.title: Rank and position puzzles
concepts.body:
Draw numbered slots (1 to 5 or 1 to 6) and place the fixed facts first.
  • "Just above", "just below", "immediately after" create blocks of people who must sit next to each other (L, H, K in order).
  • Place fixed ranks (I is first), then fit the blocks into the free slots.
  • Use "not" conditions (J is not last) to choose between the possible placements.
When a puzzle has two possible arrangements, check whether the question's answer is the same in both.

concepts.title: Top, bottom and other words
concepts.body:
• In the formulas, top, front and first all play the part of "left"; bottom, back and last play the part of "right".
  • "Ranked 5th from the top in a class" is the same as "5th from the left" in a row.
  • "Ahead of" in a queue means closer to the front.
  • In a row facing North, the person's left is the row's left end; if the row faces South, the person's left is the other end. Read which way the row faces.

varieties.name: Position from either end
varieties.how: Total = L + R − 1. Position from the other end = Total − position + 1.

example.q: Paras ranks 5th from the top and 24th from the bottom in his class. How many students are in the class?
steps: Paras is counted in both 5 and 24.

varieties.name: People between two persons
varieties.how: Convert both positions to the same end (from the left), then people between = difference − 1. Or use T − (L + R) when the two positions do not overlap.

example.q: 32 students stand in a row. Akash is 12th from the right and Priya is 18th from the left. How many people stand between them?

varieties.name: Interchanged positions
varieties.how: After a swap, A's new position equals B's old position from the same end. Use that place's two positions (left and right) to get the total.

example.q: In a row, Amit is 12th from the left and Sunil is 15th from the right. After they swap places, Amit is 17th from the left. How many people are in the row?
steps: Amit is now in Sunil's old place, so that place is 17th from the left.
The same place was 15th from the right.

varieties.name: Comparison (taller, heavier)
varieties.how: Turn each sentence into "bigger > smaller" and join them into one chain. Read the asked person from the chain.

example.q: Ramesh is taller than Qadir but shorter than Saurabh. Prakash is the shortest. Tariq is taller than Saurabh. Who is the tallest?
steps: Tariq > Saurabh, and Prakash is at the bottom.
Chain: Tariq > Saurabh > Ramesh > Qadir > Prakash.

varieties.name: Rank and position puzzles
varieties.how: Draw numbered slots. Place fixed ranks first, then blocks made by "just above" or "just below", then use the "not" conditions.

example.q: H, I, J, K and L are the top five rank holders. H is just above K and just below L. I is at the top. J is not at the lowest rank. Who is at the lowest rank?
steps: L, H, K form a block in that order (L above H above K).
I is rank 1, so ranks 2 to 5 hold the block and J.
If J were rank 5, J would be lowest, which is not allowed. So J is rank 2 and L, H, K are ranks 3, 4, 5.

tips: Total = L + R − 1. Use it for every "from both ends" question.
Convert all positions to the same end before counting people between.
After a swap, the new position belongs to the other person's old place.
For comparisons, write a single chain with the biggest on the left.
In puzzles, place fixed ranks first, then blocks, then "not" conditions.
Draw a quick line of dots for small rows; it takes less time than doubting a formula.
traps: Forgetting the − 1 in L + R − 1 (the person is counted twice).
Using T − (L + R) when the two positions overlap; then the formula is (L + R) − T − 2.
Reading "heavier than only T" as "heaviest". It means second from the bottom.
Mixing up which end a position is counted from after a swap.

questions.q: In a row of 40 students, Ram is 15th from the left end. What is his position from the right end?
In a class, Rohan is 12th from the top and 18th from the bottom. How many students are there in the class?
A is taller than B. C is shorter than B. D is taller than A. E is shorter than C. Who is in the middle when they are arranged by height?
questions.solution:
D > A (D taller than A), A > B, B > C, C > E.
Order: D > A > B > C > E.
B is in the middle.

questions.q: In a row, A is 10th from the left and B is 15th from the right. When they interchange their positions, A becomes 20th from the left. How many people are in the row?
questions.solution:
After interchange, A is at B's old place.
So B's old place is 20th from the left and 15th from the right.
Total = 20 + 15 − 1 = 34.

questions.q: In a row of 50 children, P is 18th from the left end and Q is 20th from the right end. How many children are there between P and Q?
questions.solution:
Q from the left = 50 − 20 + 1 = 31st.
P is 18th from the left.
Children between = 31 − 18 − 1 = 12.

questions.q: P, Q, R, S and T each have a different weight. Q is heavier than only T. P is heavier than R but lighter than S. Who is the heaviest?
questions.solution:
"Q is heavier than only T" → T is the lightest and Q is 4th.
The top three are P, R and S. S > P > R.
Order: S > P > R > Q > T. S is the heaviest.
